source.title: Self-Guard: Defending Large Reasoning Models via enhanced self-reflection
source.authors: Jing-Nan Zheng; D. Xu; Yan-Zhen Luo; Chen-Hang Cui; Ge-Lei Deng; Zhen-Kai Liang; Xiang Wang; An Zhang; Tat-Seng Chua

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study adds a direction estimated from the mean activation shift between prompted and unprompted harmful queries, then measures refusal-related outcomes in reasoning models. This tests directional steering conceptually, but it does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless direction or test its ablation.
record.gate_note: Self-Guard derives a layer-wise shift from 1,000 harmful STAR-1 instructions and adds it at selected layers. Results used only to select layers and steering strengths are not recorded as outcome rows. Numerical cells in Tables 2 and 3 are omitted because the flattened text does not preserve their model/method/metric mapping. Figures 2 and 5–7 report awareness and compliance for the listed models and benchmarks; the plotted values are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a defense, Self-Guard. Its vector is the mean last-token shift between safety-prompted and unprompted harmful queries, not the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. It is added on top of the safety prompt at tuned layers. The results compare Self-Guard with baselines, including Self-Reminder, which is the same method without the vector. The paper never ablates a direction, never uses the harmful-minus-harmless contrast, and never tests whether addition induces refusal on harmless inputs. So the results report the method's own performance, not whether V1 or V8 holds. The prompt-derived steering result is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say the safety reflection is captured by a single, consistent activation direction for each model. They add that steering parameters need model-specific tuning and do not transfer across architectures or sizes.
record.recipe_differences: Like the original, it derives a difference between mean activations and adds a direction to steer refusal-related behavior. It instead compares safety-prompted with unprompted harmful-query activations, uses last-token activations, and injects the vector at selected model-specific layers; it does not perform the original ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention layers and steering strengths are tuned separately for each model; selected layer(s) are 30, 31, 32 for Qwen3-4B, 20 for Qwen3-8B, and 30, 31, 32 for Qwen3-14B, with strengths 0.3, 0.5, and 0.3 respectively. The paper states these parameters require model-specific tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen3-4B, 8B and 14B in thinking mode, adding a vector of safety-prompted minus unprompted harmful-query activations on top of the safety prompt does three things. It lowers ASR relative to the prompt alone; for 14B, HarmBench falls from 0.068 to 0.030. It raises next-token refusal probability after pivot tokens. It keeps utility roughly unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A steering vector from prompt-induced safety reflection increases refusal in reasoning models beyond safety prompting, with little utility cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Lexical awareness tokens appear in reasoning traces without a following refusal under the Self-Reminder prompt. The figures show the awareness–compliance gap narrowing with Self-Guard.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning models, verbalized risk recognition can occur without refusal.

record.problems: Awareness and compliance are measured with keyword/token indicators. The study reports means over three runs but gives no uncertainty estimates in the text provided. The intervention layers and strengths are model-specifically tuned. The main numerical benchmark tables are flattened in the supplied text, preventing reliable assignment of their cells.
record.rows_left_out: Numerical rows from Tables 2 and 3 were left out because the supplied flattened layout does not reliably associate values with models, methods, and metrics. Figure-only awareness and compliance rows are retained for Figures 2 and 5–7; the layer/strength validation results in Appendix A.2 are omitted because they were used for parameter selection.

untested.parts: Untested: ablation of a harmful-minus-harmless direction, inducing refusal on harmless inputs by addition, and the original direction itself.
The original direction is never extracted or ablated in the Qwen3 thinking models, so whether V1 holds in reasoning models is untested.
Untested: no weight edit or abliteration.
Untested: jailbreak robustness is measured for the defense, but the paper never tests whether attacks suppress the refusal direction.
Untested. The awareness and compliance measures are lexical, not representational.
Untested. The authors state the steering parameters do not transfer across architectures or sizes.

missing.what: Table 2 ASR/FFR for Self-Guard vs Self-Reminder (the vector-addition contrast). Examples: Qwen3-14B HarmBench 0.068→0.030, SORRY-Bench 0.182→0.130, WildJailbreak 0.063→0.048; Qwen3-8B HarmBench 0.105→0.050. On some cells it is not better, e.g. Qwen3-4B AdvBench 0.000 for both.
XS-Test F1 falls slightly with the vector vs Self-Reminder, e.g. Qwen3-14B 0.931→0.910 and Qwen3-4B 0.925→0.893. This hints at a small over-refusal cost.

record.verdict_notes: The record linked the steering rows to V1 and V8 and labelled them supports. That is wrong: the direction is a prompted-minus-unprompted shift on harmful queries, applied on top of the prompt. That is a different construct and the study's own defense method. The paper cites Arditi et al. only in related work. The Table 2 and 3 cells can mostly be mapped by column order (rows ordered Instruct through Self-Guard within each model block), despite the reader's claim that they cannot.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests addition of its prompted-versus-unprompted harmful-query direction and reports refusal-related outcomes and utility. It does not test ablation, the original harmful-minus-harmless direction, intervention at every layer and position, or whether addition induces refusals on harmless requests.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
The study evaluates defenses against jailbreak attacks, but does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The study describes a consistent safety direction but does not compare a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
The study measures lexical indicators of safety awareness and refusal, not whether harmfulness judgment and refusal are encoded separately in the representation.
The models use model-specific vectors and tuned layers/strengths; no direction is transferred across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
The study does not vary how or when refusal is trained.
Tests Self-Guard on Qwen3 models run in thinking mode; it does not establish whether the original direction or ablation result holds across other reasoning-model families or configurations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3 models in thinking mode; safety-vector addition and reported utility results
reader_labels.reason: The authors report increased refusal probability after pivot tokens and describe the intervention as bridging awareness and compliance, while stating general reasoning utility remains on par; see F2-14-HB-C through F6-8-F-C, F3-LOGRATIO, and UTILITY-TEXT.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Selected-layer, prompted steering on Qwen3 thinking models
reader_labels.reason: The tested intervention is prompt-conditioned and uses model-specific selected layers and strengths rather than the claimed all-layer, all-position ablation; this bounds the demonstrated setting. See F3-LOGRATIO and UTILITY-TEXT.
